text:
raj: Heads-up — Skyline engineering asked for a joint perf/W + kernel-tuning run next Wed. They want throughput and joules/token across three configs: stock kernel, q4bit quant, and kv-cache enabled. Can we align on harness, telemetry schema, and a run day?

olivia: I can own the harness. Proposed minimal run command: `./bench_runner --model=redwood-4x --batch=1 --seq=2048 --warmup=200 --measure=power,latency --kvcache={on,off} --quant={none,4bit}`. Will produce p95 latency, throughput, and joules/token.

tim: Ping @skyline-eng for PDUs and kernel access. Also need clarity on OS/hypervisor: propose Ubuntu 22.04 + CUDA 12.1. If Skyline confirms, we'll schedule a slot in their lab.

jeff: Telemetry schema (short):
```json
{
  "run_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "power_w": "float",
  "tokens": "int",
  "latency_ms_p95": "float",
  "config": "string"
}
```
I'll attach a CSV exporter that maps to the schema. Use run_id for correlating kernel logs.

partner_hq_bot: Skyline: PDUs / IPMI endpoints are available. We can provide per-socket power meters and a kernel patch toggle. Available slot: 2026-04-01 09:00 PT.

nina: Quick question — do we want top-of-rack (single node) or whole-cabinet runs? Joules/token will vary a lot.

raj: Start with a single top-of-rack node for the initial sweep, then scale to 4-node cabinet if numbers look good. Olivia, please add two Grafana panels: p95 latency and joules_per_token with a run_id filter.

olivia: Will open a draft bench config + sample logs. Draft PR: https://git.redwood.com/bench/skyline/pulls/12 — it contains: run scripts, expected CSV headers, and dashboard JSON.

tim: :thumbsup: I'll create a support ticket to request Skyline lab credentials and PDU access. Jira: RED-4481 (will link).

partner_hq_bot: Skyline note — we'll attach kernel toggle v0.1 as `skyline-kpatch-v0.1.tar.gz`. It flips on our microcode affinity and a late-alloc buffer change. They recommend running stock versus kpatch for comparison.

jeff: Important: add these fields to telemetry: `kernel_version` and `pstate_profile`. Otherwise we won't differentiate kernel-induced power shifts.

raj: Agreed. Olivia, include `kernel_version` and `pstate_profile` in the exporter. Also add a small smoke test that runs `./bench_runner --smoke` to validate power meters and CSV output.

olivia: On it. Smoke-run snippet I'll include in PR:```bash
./bench_runner --model=redwood-4x --batch=1 --seq=256 --warmup=50 --measure=power,latency --smoke
```

nina: If Skyline provides kernel patch, let's gate it behind an explicit toggle in the harness so we can roll back to stock automatically. Also capture dmesg and kernel perf samples.

raj: Perfect. After Olivia's PR lands, we do a dry run internally, then coordinate with Skyline for the live lab slot. I'll follow up with a calendar invite once timelines confirmed.

olivia: Will update PR today with toggles and dashboard JSON. Expect logs and sample CSV so partner can validate parsing.

partner_hq_bot: Skyline: confirmed. We'll allocate a 4-hour slot and provide power sensor endpoints + kernel patch. We'll attach the IPMI creds in the support ticket after NDAs are signed.

raj: Thanks everyone — let's keep comms in this thread for the checklist. I'll add a short postmortem template to the PR for capturing perf vs power tradeoffs.
